title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 116
paragraphs: The Cyprians, then, after having made themselves free for a single year, had again been reduced to slavery. Meanwhile Daurises, who was married to a daughter of Darius, and Hymaees and Otanes, also Persian commanders and also married to daughters of Darius, having pursued those Ionians who had marched on Sardis and having defeated them in battle and driven them by force to their ships, divided the cities among themselves and proceeded to sack them.
